figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 3.   HPLC-­ESI-­MS analysis of in vitro KSA 
and KSB reactions. The reactions with (A) 
C2-­ACP/malonyl-­ACP, (B) C4-­ACP/malonyl-­
ACP, (C) C6-­ACP/malonyl-­ACP, (D) C8-­ACP/
malonyl-­ACP, (E) C10-­ACP/malonyl-­ACP, (F) 
C12-­ACP/malonyl-­ACP, (G) C14-­ACP/malonyl-­
ACP, (H) C18-­ACP/malonyl-­ACP, and (I) C20-­
ACP/malonyl-­ACP. Substrates for C8 to C10 
(D), C14 to C16 (G), and C20 to C22 (I) elon-
gations were prepared in situ with combina-
tion reactions. Top, without enzyme; Middle, 
with KSA; and Bottom, with KSB. Total ion 
chromatograms (Left) and deconvoluted ESI-­
TOF-­MS spectra of the substrate/product at 
the retention time marked with a red double-­
head arrow (Right) are shown. Malonyl-­ACP 
and holo-­ACP are marked with a diamond 
and asterisk, respectively. The enzymatically 
prepared C8-­, C14-­, and C20-­ACP substrates 
were detected as 3-­hydroxyacyl-­ACP because 
3-­hydroxyacyl-­ACP is more thermodynamical-
ly stable than 2-­cis-­acyl-­ACP formed by dehy-
dration/isomerization reactions with DHFabA 
(SI Appendix, Scheme S2).
